candidate_rules.note: Normalizes the Date.now() epoch-millisecond cache-buster query values to a constant, covering D-cache-buster (588 HTML files at 2cda2bdda6b7).

Masks the nondeterministic prev/next pagination hrefs (D-category-order). This redacts rather than normalizes: the category order varies run to run via the TemplateMap async race, so no regex can recover a canonical order.

differences.mechanism: src/site/humans.html renders Last update via getCurrentDate filter (.eleventy.js / eleventy/filters.js), which formats the local new Date() as YYYY/MM/DD. b3 runs under TZ=Pacific/Auckland, where the wall-clock date is one day ahead of UTC, so the rendered date differs.

eleventy/index.js sets buildTimestamp = Date.now() (refreshed on eleventy.before) and exposes it as global data build.timestamp; src/site/_includes/head.html appends ?v={{ build.timestamp }} to three CSS links. Every build gets a fresh epoch-millisecond value. Representative regions use b1 vs b2; b3 carries ?v=1790346670605 and b4 its own value.

differences.mechanism: src/site/category.html paginates over the collections object (pagination.data: collections); Eleventy resolves this via Object.keys(collections), i.e. tag-collection insertion order. Insertion order comes from TemplateMap._testGetAllTags() iterating this.map, and this.map is populated by concurrent templateMap.add() calls (TemplateWriter pushes templateMap.add(tmpl) promises and awaits Promise.all), each of which awaits template.getData() before pushing. Push order therefore follows async data-resolution order, which varies run to run. Observed orders: b1 javascript->approach->skill->service->speaking; b2 javascript->approach->service->speaking->skill; b3 javascript->approach->speaking->skill->service. Representative regions use b1 vs b2 on category/approach.html.

differences.files_note: 22 pagefind index chunk files per build carry content-hash names (en_<hash>.pf_index); all 22 names differ between b1 and b2/b3. pagefind-entry.json references the index hash. b4's pagefind output is byte-identical to b1's (verified: 403 files, zero differing), so b4 is excluded. Representative region quotes pagefind-entry.json b1 vs b2.
differences.mechanism: eleventy/build.js runs pagefind --site dist after the Eleventy build. Pagefind names index chunks and the entry hash by content hash (en_<hash>); the hashes take two values across the four builds (b1/b4: en_89774e10a2; b2/b3: en_2027d70c77). The indexed page fragments themselves are byte-identical across b1/b2 (verified), so the hash inputs exclude page body text; the exact pagefind-internal hash input was not isolated.
